subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain its own batch STT backend boundary, and should that boundary call Gateway tools.media.audio, Talk transcription providers, or a new native/provider contract?
rationale: The source proves the capability is missing, but implementing it safely requires a product and security decision about native capture ownership, provider selection, credentials, private-network access, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Design native PTT batch STT seam
options.body: Add a maintainer-scoped PTT-only backend abstraction with Apple Speech as default and a first approved Gateway/media-audio bridge for final transcripts.

options.title: Fold into broader native ASR issue
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 as the canonical design packet and keep this issue as the macOS PTT-specific acceptance slice.

options.title: Route to plugin-only surfaces
options.body: Do not add native PTT backend surface unless a plugin or provider API gap is proven after attempting the existing media/realtime provider seams.

recommendation.title: Design native PTT batch STT seam
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-scoped PTT-only backend abstraction with Apple Speech as default and a first approved Gateway/media-audio bridge for final transcripts.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest native macOS voice history signal and is the best available owner for the native app product/API boundary choice.
